sentences.text: 1. This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for claiming compensation on account of death of Shivaraju S/o Late Krishnappa.

2. It is the case of the petitioners that on 29.11.2022 at about 2.00 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Tavarekere 3 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 Police Station, at NICE Road Junction, Bengaluru - Magadi main road, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North taluk, the deceased rider/Manjunath riding the unoffending TVS Jupitor Scooter bearing registration No.KA-05-LG-4416 along with deceased Shivaraju as a pillion rider from Doddagollarahatti towards Chikkagollarahatti and at 'U'
turn of the NICE road junction while taking 'U' turn by giving indication and signal to the following vehicles at that time the driver/ accused of the offending BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-995 drove the same from Bengaluru towards Magadi side in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result both rider and pillion rider fallen on the left side of the road and the front side right wheel and rear wheel of the offending Bus run over the heads of the both rider and pillion rider as a result they have sustained grievous injuries and both were died on the spot.
Thereafter, the informant/Ravikumar.L lodged complaint before the Tavarekere police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.390/2022 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and 4 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint it is seen that on 29.11.2022 at about 2.00 p.m., at NICE Road Junction, Bengaluru - Magadi main road, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North taluk, the deceased rider/Manjunath riding the unoffending TVS Jupitor Scooter bearing registration No.KA-05-LG-4416 along with deceased Shivaraju as a pillion rider from Doddagollarahatti towards Chikkagollarahatti and at 'U' turn of the NICE road junction while taking 'U' turn by giving indication and signal to the following vehicles at 16 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 that time the driver/accused of the offending BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-995 drove the same from Bengaluru towards Magadi side in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result both rider and pillion rider fallen on the left side of the road and the front side right wheel and rear wheel of the offending Bus run over the heads of the both rider and pillion rider as a result they have sustained grievous injuries and both were died on the spot.
The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the driver of the offending BMTC vehicle.

22. The Respondent No.1 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and counsel further contended that the alleged accident occurred due fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the accused and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the deceased unoffending vehicle as a result deceased sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.
In view of the police records, it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the deceased Shivaraju died due to 18 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 injuries sustained in the alleged accident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Shivaraju noted in the Ex.P7/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 304A of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent young man/Shivaraju aforesaid, as the driver of offending vehicle/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

26. It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent 20 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
In the instance case the petitioners claimed that deceased was doing Solar fitting work and earning an income of Rs.20,000/- p.m.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the actual income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the deceased taken at Rs.14,750/-.

The Petitioners No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of the deceased, in view of the law laid down by the constitution bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.

sentences.text: Thus the 40% of the future prospects is to be added, hence the monthly income comes to Rs.20,650/- (Rs.14,750/- + 40% = 5,900).

Since the deceased is the bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% towards personal and living expenses and remaining amount, i.e.,
Rs.10,325/- (Rs.20,650/- - Rs.10,325/-) has to be taken as his/deceased contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 28 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.
Thus the claimants are entitled to compensation of 21 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 Rs.21,06,300/- (Rs.10,325/- x 12 x 17) on account of loss of dependency.
27. In addition, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the sister and Petitioner No.2 is the brother of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.

opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:-
Nagarathnamma vs The Managing Director, Bmtc on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96587291/
3 :: I S S U E S ::
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that deceased Shivaraju S/o Late Krishnappa sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of driving of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-995 7 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 dated 29.11.2022 at about 2.00 p.m.,
and succumbed to injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Shivaraju S/o Late Krishnappa?
4. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
5. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, deceased was dead due to grievous injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending BMTC Bus vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the deceased unoffending vehicle as a result deceased sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.
In view of the police records, it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the deceased Shivaraju died due to 18 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 injuries sustained in the alleged accident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Shivaraju noted in the Ex.P7/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 304A of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent young man/Shivaraju aforesaid, as the driver of offending vehicle/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 28 years.
In the instance case the petitioners claimed that deceased was doing Solar fitting work and earning an income of Rs.20,000/- p.m.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the actual income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the deceased taken at Rs.14,750/-.
The Petitioners No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of the deceased, in view of the law laid down by the constitution bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 25. The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 27 years and the petitioners relied on the Ex.P-7/Postmortem report of the deceased, wherein the age of the deceased is shown as 28 years.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus the 40% of the future prospects is to be added, hence the monthly income comes to Rs.20,650/- (Rs.14,750/- + 40% = 5,900).
Since the deceased is the bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% towards personal and living expenses and remaining amount, i.e.,
Rs.10,325/- (Rs.20,650/- - Rs.10,325/-) has to be taken as his/deceased contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 28 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.
Thus the claimants are entitled to compensation of 21 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 Rs.21,06,300/- (Rs.10,325/- x 12 x 17) on account of loss of dependency.
27. In addition, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the sister and Petitioner No.2 is the brother of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.
Thus the Petitioners are entitled to the following compensation:
28.
The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl.
No. Compensation under Amount in (Rs) different heads 1 Loss of dependency 21,06,300.00 2 Funeral Expenses 15,000.00 3 Loss of Estate 15,000.00 4 Loss of filial consortium 80,000.00 5 Loss of love and affection 1,00,000.00
Total 23,16,300.00 22 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 29.
The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.23,16,300/-.
30.
Hence the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.1/ RC owner and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the RC owner/Respondent No.1 is directed to the deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.3 in the affirmative and issue No.2 and 4 partly in the affirmative.

9 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.23,16,300/-
(Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Sixteen Thousand and Three Hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
23 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.849/2023 Further, Respondent No.1 being RC owner of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6%
interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of total compensation amount, the Petitioner No.2 is entitled for 50% share with interest, the Petitioners No.3 is entitled for 50% share with interest.
After deposit, entire share of compensation amount with interest shall be released in their favour through E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
